chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who bequeathed a 'portion' of his wealth, so he said:
Due to the Words of Allah, Blessed and High,

Indeed, the charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials (appointed) over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer.

key_terms.وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ: And those whose hearts are reconciled
key_terms.وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: And in the cause of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the specific fraction of wealth defined as a 'portion' (sahm) in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the term 'portion' (sahm) in bequests refers specifically to one-eighth, directly linking it to the eight categories of recipients listed in Surah At-Tawbah (9:60). This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving precise legal fractions from Quranic terminology, ensuring that bequests align with the broader principles of Zakat distribution. The ruling provides clarity for testators, distinguishing this specific bequest category from the general shares allocated to heirs.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who bequeathed with a ‘portion’ of his wealth. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The ‘portion’ is one from eight (1/8) due to the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High

[9:60] But rather, the charities are only for the poor and the needy, and the officials (appointed) over them, and those whose hearts are made to incline (to Truth) and the (ransoming of) captives and those in debts and in the Way of Allah and the wayfarer
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who makes a will about a share of his legacy. He (the Imam) said, ‘A share is one-eighth because of the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, “Charity is only for the poor, destitute, Zakat collectors, people inclined to the religion, slaves, debtors, in the way of Allah and for those who deplete their supplies on journey.’”” [9:60]
